text: 54-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing a gradual difficulty in walking over the past 3 months, requiring wheelchair assistance for the last month. speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the combination of gait disturbance, incontinence, and dysarthria is very specific. Given your age and the progressive nature of these symptoms, have you noticed any changes in your handwriting or muscle cramps/spasms in your arms or legs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive difficulty walking. I also have Urinary incontinence, Slurred speech, Rigidity in limbs, Mild hand tremor, Orthostatic hypotension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain and MRI Cervical Spine.
REQUEST IMAGES.
These specific findings of rigidity, tremor, autonomic dysfunction (orthostatic hypotension), and urinary incontinence alongside gait disturbance strongly suggest a neurodegenerative disorder affecting both the brainstem and spinal cord; I need to visualize the pons and cervical spine to confirm the diagnosis.
